**ACCEPT** — PR #8787.

## My mechanism assumption was not just wrong, it was unbuildable

I dispatched this with: *"route `searchAll` through the same `resolveSearchFields` / `expandSearchToFilter` the `$search` executor uses"*, and invited falsification on whether per-object helpers could serve a cross-object sweep.

The per-object worry was unfounded — *"the sweep was already a loop of per-object `engine.find` calls, so the per-object expansion fits exactly where the old per-object filter sat."* But the import half is **impossible**:

> `expandSearchToFilter` lives in `@objectstack/objectql`, which **depends on** `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`. Importing it would close a package cycle.

So the routing went one level **up** instead: `searchAll` hands `engine.find` the query **text** (`search: q`, a declared `find` option) per object, and the engine expands it. That leaves **one producer of search clauses** rather than two that agree by maintenance — which is strictly better than the shared-helper shape I proposed, and it is the version that survives someone changing the expansion later.

**Also: my region declaration was stale.** I claimed `searchAll` at `~:7177–7411`; it is at `:8520–8700`. The dev re-derived from the tree rather than trusting my claim comment, which is what the rule says to do and why no conflict occurred.

## A fourth axis, found *by* the ablation

The reverse verification predicted 5 red / 8 green and measured **6 red / 7 green** — divergence declared rather than smoothed. The extra red is how this was found:

> the old fallback chain ended in "the first text-typed field", which on an object whose only text column is its PK selects `id` — so **every keystroke ran `{id: {$icontains: term}}` against system/junction/log tables**.

That is #4483's defect, which the executor had already fixed and this path had not. So the PR carries a **narrowing** alongside the three widenings, and it exists because an ablation disagreed with a prediction. Those objects are now skipped.

## The pin measures the right thing

> The load-bearing assertion is **parity**, not "the palette finds pinyin": a palette widened by narrowing the executor would satisfy the latter and is a failure.

That is the direction I asked to be protected, and it is protected by comparing both paths against each other **and** against a written expectation, with the per-object filter each hands the driver compared **tree-to-tree**. A test that only asserted "pinyin now works" would have passed on a change that broke the executor.

**The first ablation came back all-green and was declared invalid** — the `dist` resolution trap again — and both legs were re-run with `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` proving the mutation reached the artifact. Fourth dev tonight to hit that trap; every one of them disclosed it rather than banking the false green.

## #7850, and a pleasing recursion

Row 3 (*"case-insensitive substring matching via `$contains`"*) was **already corrected on `main`** by #7641's landing — so **the card's own root-cause paragraph naming it as stale is itself now stale**. Row 2 (*"case-insensitive LIKE"*) was still there and is corrected: `LIKE` names no operator in this vocabulary and, since #6518's LIKE→GLOB change, not even the SQL the compilers emit.

Left alone as instructed: #7850 row 1 (spec seat's, card stays open for it) and `search-filter.ts:18`, correct as a declaration under #4706 Q2 = A.

## Housekeeping

- **#8786 filed, not fixed** — `renderTitle` in this same function reads only the deprecated `displayNameField`, never the canonical `nameField`, while `provisionPrimary` stamps only the latter. Titling, not recall. Correct call to leave it.
- `check:type-check-debt` caught a **+1 in the dev's own new test** (`Array.prototype.at` outside this package's tsc `lib`) — **fixed rather than raised**. Ledger flat at 1968.
- Four consumer suites run, not just the two changed packages: `metadata-protocol`, `objectql`, `rest`, `runtime`. That is the sweep whose absence cost us the #8770 regression tonight.

Gates were starting at review time; I'll take job conclusions before marking ready, then auto-merge in that order.

**Docs check — no change needed, and the reason is worth recording: the published docs already describe the behaviour this PR ships.**

I checked this one properly rather than waving the advisory away, because unlike tonight's other PRs it genuinely changes what a published endpoint returns — and because the drift check demonstrably missed the documenting page on #8421 today.

**Every `searchable` hit in the docs is object-level**, inside the `enable: { … }` capability block ("Include in global search index" / "Index records for global search"). That is the object sweep, which this PR leaves unchanged. No doc describes the *field-level* `searchable: true` flag as selecting which fields global search matches — which is the thing this PR stops honouring.

And `content/docs/data-modeling/schema-design.mdx:86-88` states the field-selection rule outright:

> `searchable: true` includes an object's records in global search and the record picker. **By default the search matches the name/title field plus short-text fields. To control exactly which fields are matched, set `searchableFields` on the object (ADR-0061).**

That is precisely what this PR implements — declared `searchableFields`, else the auto-default. So **the docs were already right and `searchAll` was wrong**; this PR brings the code into line with the published contract rather than moving the contract.

That is a useful corroboration of the PR's direction from a source the dev did not cite: `references/data/object.mdx:140` likewise already named global search as one of `searchableFields`' three consumers, which the PR body notes it *makes* true.

(Reverse control on the search: 97 doc files mention "search", so the absence of a field-level claim is a real absence, not a broken grep.)
